iterations.learnings_appended_to_agents_md: yes — (1) check_fn should accept Promise<boolean> as well as boolean (some prereqs are async probes — e.g. LSP server reachable, MCP server connected). (2) Defence-in-depth dispatch guard is mandatory: the LLM can emit tool calls to tools not in its schema (especially when context-compacted), so the dispatch path must re-check availability. (3) SelfRegisteringToolRegistry already had its own checkFn plumbing via opts — unifying via `opts.checkFn ?? tool.check_fn` avoids forcing callers to register check_fn in two places. (4) Gemini-cli uses a different paradigm (PolicyRule with TOML + argsPattern RegExp + decision: ALLOW/DENY/ASK_USER) — appropriate for arg-pattern gating, but verbose for the common "service-not-configured" case; Goli keeps check_fn for service-gating and uses PreToolUse hooks (block_destructive, block_secrets) for arg-pattern gating.
